Hi Aditya,

Thanks again for the demo earlier today — really helpful. A few follow-ups from our security and platform teams while we qualify Redwood for our customer-facing assistants: 

- Can you confirm whether PII (user inputs / generated outputs) can be restricted to a single region (US) and that backups are kept in-region by default?
- What are the defaults for logging retention (event logs, request traces, model inputs) and can we opt to disable persistent storage of model inputs?

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>

Hi Liam —

Appreciate the clear list. Short recap and next steps below; Marissa will add technical specifics. Attaching our Region Pinning FAQ and SOC2 attestation (see attachments).

Recap / answers at a high level:
- Region pinning: yes — we support tenant-level region pinning. You can choose a primary region (e.g., us-east-1) where all model inputs/outputs and ephemeral caches are routed and stored.
- Backups: by default backups and snapshots are stored in the same primary region. Cross-region replication is available as an opt-in service for DR.
- Logging retention: default request logs are retained for 30 days; audit logs for 365 days. We can configure shorter retention or disable persisting model inputs on a per-customer basis (useful for PII minimization).
- Cross-region failover: implemented via asynchronous replication to a configured DR region. Typical RTO is in the range of minutes (3–10 mins) depending on session state; RPO depends on replication window. If strict synchronous replication is required, we can discuss Dedicated deployment options and the cost/latency tradeoffs.
- EU-only residency: routing and storage can be constrained to EU regions; note that cross-region backups or failover to non-EU regions will not be enabled unless explicitly requested and contracted. There may be a pricing delta for EU-only dedicated pools.

Next steps:
1) Marissa to confirm specific retention windows, KV/ prefix cache persistence, and the replication mechanics for backups.
2) We'll produce a short mutual action plan + a draft SOW line for EU-only residency and dedicated DR.
3) Please let me know if procurement wants a one-page confirmation for their questionnaire or a full security package.

Marissa / Sean — can you add the technical details (replication mode, default retention, KMS options) inline?

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Follow-up — region pinning questions

Hi all — quick technical details to supplement Aditya's notes:

- Tenant-level region pinning: requests are routed at the control plane to worker pools in the selected region. Model inputs/outputs and short-term KV cache are kept in-region by default.
- Backups & snapshots: we create daily snapshots kept in the primary region. Retention policy is configurable; default is 30 days for snapshots and 90 days for longer-term backups (if enabled). Backups are NOT automatically replicated out-of-region unless cross-region DR is enabled.
- Cross-region failover: we use asynchronous replication for DR. Replication is incremental; RTO typically 3–5 minutes for stateless endpoints, up to 10–15 minutes for stateful sessions depending on cache size. RPO is configurable (depends on replication frequency).
- PII and logs: request/response persistence is configurable. For customers requiring minimal retention we can: 1) disable request logging, 2) redact or truncate model inputs before storing, and 3) disable long-term KV persistence.
- Key management & encryption: data at rest is encrypted using customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM integrations available for Dedicated/Private). TLS for data in transit.
- Audit & access logs: available via the Console and can be exported to your log sink (SIEM) or delivered via secure S3 (EU endpoints available). Default audit log retention is 365 days; shorter windows can be configured contractually.

I'll draft a short doc that states: 1) primary region storage, 2) backups in-region by default, 3) cross-region failover available only when enabled, and 4) options to disable/purge model inputs.

\u0014Marissa
Director, Applied ML & Inference
Redwood Inference

Hi Liam —

Thanks — quick summary and action items below. We're aligned and can provide the written confirmations you requested. Attachments: Redwood-Region-Pinning-FAQ.pdf and SOC2-Attestation-2025.pdf (attached).

Summary confirmations we'll provide as a short letter for procurement/security:
- EU-only residency: when selected and contracted, all customer data (model inputs/outputs, backups, snapshots, logs) will remain in EU regions. Cross-region replication to non-EU regions will not be enabled without explicit, documented customer authorization.
- Disable request persistence: we offer a configurable short retention buffer (default 48 hours) for troubleshooting which can be disabled. If persistence is disabled, debugging will be limited to live session traces; we can discuss secure on-demand capture workflows for incident investigations.
- Pricing delta: for EU-only dedicated pools expect a ballpark increase of ~15–25% compared to mixed-region hosted pricing; exact number depends on instance types, committed throughput, and whether DR (cross-region replication) is required. We'll include a ballpark estimate in the SOW snippet.
